reason: I don't buy dev tools without checking Reddit, GitHub issues, and Twitter first, and Loom is brand new—no reviews, no track record, just a founding-member pre-sale and a personal homebrew tap. The shared-context pitch fits my 3+ agent setup, but I'm not paying $30 a seat for something I can't vet, and running another local daemon is one more thing that can break.
objection: It's too new and unproven; I read every review before buying and there's nothing to read, plus I'd have to run and manage loomd myself.
would_change_my_mind: Independent reviews from engineering leads actually running it in production on Reddit or GitHub, plus a free trial before I pay.
